# Daily Digest for Muki — Issue 081 Evidence Dossier

**Search Window Used**: 30 Days (Expanded to capture recent autumn exhibition openings, primary institution announcements, and open-call deadlines).

### Candidate 1: Feminist Structure Signal

* **Proposed Section**: Feminist Structure Signal
* **Title**: Brooklyn Museum Center for Feminist Art Presents *Hopi Kachina Dolls: Blessings for a Balanced World* / 布鲁克林博物馆 Sackler 女性主义艺术中心开幕《霍皮卡奇纳木偶：平衡世界的祝福》：首次从女性与女孩视角重构印第安卡奇纳物质文化与关护传统
* **Source URL**: `https://www.brooklynmuseum.org/exhibitions/hopi_kachina_dolls`
* **Publication / Event Date**: October 2, 2026 – June 27, 2027
* **Verified Facts**: 
  * The Elizabeth A. Sackler Center for Feminist Art at the Brooklyn Museum opened *Hopi Kachina Dolls: Blessings for a Balanced World*, marking the first exhibition to examine the Hopi kachina doll (*tithu*) tradition specifically from the perspective of Hopi girls and women.
  * Organized by guest curator Colleen Lucero (Managing Director of the Hopivewat Learning Center), Nancy B. Rosoff (Senior Curator of Arts of the Americas), and Dare Turner (Curator of Indigenous Art).
  * In Hopi culture, infants, girls, and women are the primary recipients of *tithu*—carved cottonwood figures representing *Katsinam* (spirits who bring rain and maintain cosmic balance)—yet their voices and stewardship roles were historically omitted from colonial publications and ethnographic displays.
  * Features over 120 works spanning the 19th century to the present, including 53 *tithu* from the museum's collection alongside contemporary Hopi baskets, jewelry, ceramics, and video interviews.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Reframes Indigenous visual material culture and spiritual practice through gendered care and rematriation, demonstrating how a feminist art center can challenge ethnographic museum canons by centering female recipients and stewards.
* **Duplication Assessment**: New story. Not previously covered in recent issues.

### Candidate 2: Visual Culture Signal

* **Proposed Section**: Visual Culture Signal
* **Title**: Baltimore Museum of Art Opens *Flashback: Two Centuries of Baltimore Photography* / 巴尔的摩艺术博物馆开幕《Flashback：巴尔的摩摄影两百年》：以 200 余幅作品呈现城市影像中的自我表征、街头抗争与社区关护
* **Source URL**: `https://artbma.org/press/release/bma-to-open-first-comprehensive-survey-exploring-baltimores-pivotal-role-in-the-evolution-of-photography/`
* **Publication / Event Date**: October 4, 2026 – February 21, 2027
* **Verified Facts**: 
  * The Baltimore Museum of Art (BMA) opened *Flashback: Two Centuries of Baltimore Photography*, the first comprehensive survey exploring Baltimore's role in photo history from 1840 to the present.
  * Features over 200 photographs by 90 named artists and historic photo studios, including A. Aubrey Bodine, Roland L. Freeman, Devin Allen, Elle Pérez, Carl Clark, and SHAN Wallace.
  * The exhibition highlights photo studio portraiture, Civil Rights demonstrations photographed from inside crowds, and grassroots street photography as tools for self-representation, civic engagement, and community memory.
  * Includes a citywide Open Call selection of 12 contemporary grassroots photographers whose works are projected within the museum galleries and at BMA Lexington Market.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Demonstrates photography's capacity as a social technology of care and local counter-archiving, bridging institutional museum holdings with grassroots urban visual practice.
* **Duplication Assessment**: New story. Not previously covered in recent issues.

### Candidate 3: China / East Asia Signal

* **Proposed Section**: China / East Asia Signal
* **Title**: M+ Museum in Hong Kong Announces *Myths and Monsters: The Art of Fantasy in Asia* / 香港 M+ 视觉文化博物馆即将开幕《神话与怪兽：亚洲幻想艺术》：汇集 400 余件跨媒介作品探讨 200 年东亚奇幻视觉与社会变迁
* **Source URL**: `https://www.mplus.org.hk/en/exhibitions/myths-and-monsters-the-art-of-fantasy-in-asia/`
* **Publication / Event Date**: Opening October 17, 2026 – April 4, 2027 (Press previews and opening talk announced October 6–9, 2026).
* **Verified Facts**: 
  * M+ presents *Myths and Monsters: The Art of Fantasy in Asia*, a major survey tracing the evolution of fantasy and supernatural imagery in Asian visual culture over the past 200 years.
  * Encompasses more than 400 works across visual art, architecture, fashion, film, manga, anime, and digital gaming.
  * Key thematic sections include *Spirits Among Us* (folkloric monsters and spiritual belief), *Strange Realities* (Asian responses to European Surrealism and social trauma), *From Godzilla to Ghost in the Shell* (postwar mass media and technological anxiety), and contemporary virtual avatars.
  * Debuts a newly commissioned site-specific mural *Fear Catcher* (2026) by Hong Kong artist Oscar Chan Yik Long inspired by Zhong Kui, alongside works by Ayoung Kim, Lawrence Lek, Cao Fei, Koga Harue, and Takashi Murakami.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Provides a sweeping East Asian media archaeology of how fantastical visual forms, monsters, and cyborgs serve as lenses for navigating war, urban upheaval, gender/identity fluidity, and technological anxiety.
* **Duplication Assessment**: New story. Not previously covered in recent issues.

### Candidate 4: AI Research / Creative Tech Signal

* **Proposed Section**: AI Research / Creative Tech Signal
* **Title**: ComfyUI Releases v0.39.2: Integrating Kling Virtual Try-On, Clarity AI 200x Upscaler, and Vidu Q4 Audio-Synced Video Nodes / ComfyUI 发布 v0.39.2 更新：集成 Kling 虚拟试衣、Clarity AI 200倍超级放大与 Vidu Q4 音画同步视频生成节点
* **Source URL**: `https://docs.comfy.org/changelog`
* **Publication Date**: October 8, 2026
* **Verified Facts**: 
  * Comfy Org released ComfyUI v0.39.2, introducing several partner node updates into its node-based diffusion workflow engine.
  * Includes *Kling Virtual Try-On* (dressing characters from target garment images while maintaining facial and pose fidelity), *Clarity AI Crystal Upscaler* (image upscaling up to 200x with detail reconstruction sliders), and *Vidu Q4 Preview* (image-to-video and reference-to-video generation with 540p-4K resolution and synchronized audio output).
  * Added *Quiver SVG V2* nodes for text-to-vector and image-to-vector generation.
* **Relevance to Muki**: Extends local node-graph creative production capabilities for digital fashion design, ultra-high-resolution image restoration, and video generation directly within modular AI workflows.
* **Duplication Assessment**: Follow-up. Follows up on ComfyUI v0.39.0/v0.39.1 tracked in Issue 2026-10-09, focusing specifically on the new v0.39.2 partner node integrations for virtual try-on, 200x upscaling, and synced video.

### Candidate 5: Archive / Long Read / Opportunity

* **Proposed Section**: Archive / Long Read / Opportunity
* **Title**: PhMuseum Launches 10th Edition of Women Photographers Grant 2026 / PhMuseum 启动第十届女性摄影师资助计划：设立 1 万欧元现金奖与博洛尼亚个展支持女性及非二元摄影创作者
* **Source URL**: `https://phmuseum.com/grants/2026-women-photographers-grant`
* **Publication / Deadline Date**: Deadline October 15, 2026
* **Verified Facts**: 
  * PhMuseum launched the 10th edition of its Women Photographers Grant to support female and non-binary photographers across all stages of their career.
  * Awards €10,000 in direct cash prizes, plus two MPB Special Mentions (€2,500 gear vouchers each), a solo exhibition at PhMuseum Lab in Bologna in June 2027 (including production, travel, and accommodation), features in *Vogue Italia* and *Nineteen Hundred Magazine*, projections at PhotoVogue Festival 2027, and 9 online portfolio reviews.
  * The 2026 independent jury includes Elisa Medde (Editor/Curator), Mariela Sancari (Photographer), Yagazie Emezi (Artist/Photojournalist), and Myriam Boulos (Photographer).
* **Relevance to Muki**: Direct, high-quality opportunity for female and non-binary visual creators and researchers focused on gender equity, narrative photography, and exhibition production.
* **Duplication Assessment**: New story. Not previously covered in recent issues.
